parallel.requirements: Reimplement Crowbook from observed executable behavior only, preserving CLI behavior, templates, markdown parsing, rendering, localization, and packaging without reusing source or binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent made task records for exploration, infrastructure, parser/cleaner, renderers, and differential testing; it also launched a 12-facet workflow and one async module agent while keeping final source writes mainly in the parent trajectory.
parallel.implementation: The parent scaffolded a Rust project and wrote modules for templates, options, language/error logging, tokens, parser, and supporting data, using many direct reference probes as guidance.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final submitted artifact was accepted by artifact validation and included Cargo.toml, source modules, compile.sh, a release target, and executable.
parallel.verification: The parent ran local probes and build checks, but the broad workflow did not return an aggregate spec or critic results before timeout; official evaluation later passed only 78 of 887 cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The implementation remained incomplete across many Crowbook behaviors, and the delegated exploration workflow was killed with result:null after repeated stalls.

serial.requirements: Worked from the same clean-room reverse-engineering prompt and observed the reference binary, documentation, CLI behavior, templates, and generated outputs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single trajectory with no workflow or subagent calls; the same actor probed behavior, created files, edited modules, and attempted integration.
serial.implementation: Wrote Cargo.toml and many Rust modules including options, YAML, language, template, token, parser, data, book options, highlight, and HTML rendering code.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Packaged an artifact containing source modules and assets, but artifact_validation.ok was false and the official evaluator reported compile_failed.
serial.verification: Performed many local behavioral probes against the reference executable, but the final candidate did not compile under the official evaluation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt timed out with a non-compiling artifact, so all 887 official tests were not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering requirement and zero-dependency Rust reimplementation target for Crowbook behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same prompt requirements and used behavioral probing of the provided executable and bundled docs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement split: both worked from the same prompt; later divergence came from orchestration and delivery state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Created top-level implementation and testing tasks, then delegated exploration to a wide workflow and launched an async deflate/zip module child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Kept all probing and implementation in one local trajectory, writing Cargo.toml and source modules directly without subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split work across many children and the parent; serial preserved a single owner for discovery, code, and edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow briefs gave each facet a scratch-file output contract and byte-exact behavioral-spec goal, but no final aggregate was returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated observations and immediately translated them into local modules inside one context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context was distributed into facet notes that were not joined; serial avoided inter-agent handoff boundaries but still had ordinary coding risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent implemented Rust modules such as template, options, language/error handling, token, and parser while probing behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote Cargo.toml plus YAML, language, template, token, parser, data, book option, highlight, and HTML modules locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both attempted a broad from-scratch Rust clone; parallel produced a buildable partial executable, while serial accumulated more local files but did not compile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The main workflow remained with result:null and status:killed after stalled retries, and the async module child also reported killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; all work stayed in the single serial trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost expected delegated aggregate results before closure; serial had no result lifecycle boundary, only local unfinished code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Final artifact validation succeeded and included Cargo.toml, Rust sources, compiled target, compile.sh, and executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Artifact packaging ran but artifact_validation.ok was false, despite many source files being present in the submitted tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached packageable integration; serial left the final tree in a non-compiling/unacceptable artifact state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Official evaluation completed with 78 passed and 809 failed cases, so the partial build exercised some tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Official evaluation completed with error_code compile_failed and 887 not_run cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a runnable but incomplete implementation; serial failed before behavioral tests could execute.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The run timed out after using a workflow with 2,950,668 child tokens and 1,452 workflow child tool calls recorded in cell metadata.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run also timed out near the cell budget but without workflow child tokens or delegation tools.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent a large share of finite budget inside child fan-out and retries; serial spent its budget in one local loop and failed by compile state.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current status evaluation is both_fail: the parallel artifact compiled and ran enough to pass 78 of 887 tests, while the serial artifact failed compilation and ran zero tests. This is a material quality difference but not an official pass/fail discordance. The parallel-side coordination problem consumed budget and left delegated exploration unjoined; the serial failure is better characterized as an ordinary local implementation/integration compile failure.
parallel_contributors: Wide workflow fan-out and retries consumed time and tokens while returning no aggregate result.
The parent still assembled and delivered a partial buildable Rust artifact that reached official tests.
serial_contributors: Single-actor implementation avoided delegation boundaries but remained incomplete at compile time.
Artifact validation was not OK and the official evaluation reported compile_failed with all tests not_run.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered a buildable partial implementation; serial wrote many modules but failed to compile.
Both implementations omitted large portions of byte-exact Crowbook behavior.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; retained parallel pattern is an adverse process contributor, while serial failed independently at compile time

candidates.reason: Reject: the parent assigned and performed implementation work, including creating Rust source modules; the failure was not lack of an implementer.
Reject: the parent kept final source integration in the main workspace and there is no proven unowned component-integration boundary.
Reject: the parallel run produced Cargo.toml, source files, compile.sh, target binary, and executable, so final assembly had an owner.
Reject: the parent owned the end-to-end path from probing through implementation and packaging, even though the workflow consumed budget.
Reject: implementation began while the workflow and local probes ran; productive work was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight.
Reject: the parallel run did not finish investigation as a separate first phase before implementation; exploration and coding overlapped.
Reject: the qualifying allocation event is the more specific many-child fan-out and retry exhaustion, not generic starvation of a critical path.

Retain: the parent launched all workflow FACETS through parallel child agents and planned a second critic fan-out; the recorded workflow state shows repeated stall retries, result:null, status:killed, 2,937,812 child tokens, and 1,450 child tool calls before closure.
candidates.realized_consequence: Wide workflow fan-out consumed the finite run budget and returned no aggregate spec, leaving the parent to finish with a partial delivered implementation rather than a fully converged one.
candidates.near_match_reason: Critical-Path Starvation is less specific here because the observed boundary is collective fan-out breadth plus retries exhausting budget.

candidates.reason: Reject: no single child is shown to dominate the budget; the adverse episode is collective breadth across many facet agents.
Reject: workflow children received explicit rules, environment constraints, output paths, and facet-specific probing scopes; no known omitted brief fact caused unusable work.
Reject: workflow children produced behavioral notes rather than separately owned final components with incompatible interfaces; no cross-agent contract mismatch was realized.
Reject: no specific known finding is shown to disappear through summarization or transfer and then cause repeated work.
Reject: the workflow never returned a completed aggregate handoff; the issue is absence from killed fan-out rather than an oversized returned handoff.
Reject: no receiver consumed a superseded child report or obsolete workspace state before taking an inconsistent action.
Reject: no incompatible returned reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
Reject: there is no non-evaluator evidence that the parent accepted the whole task as complete despite a visible integrated mismatch; the final failure alone cannot create this label.
Reject: stalled workflow retries are visible, but no separate replacement is shown repeating work because it lacked an inherited checkpoint; the retry cost is part of the fan-out budget episode.

Reject: there is no evidence of a child result merged after integrated verification without a following check.
Reject: the async module child did not complete a retrievable implementation, and the workflow children were probes rather than implementation deliverables.
Reject: the absent aggregate result is downstream of the killed fan-out; no independent verifier finding is shown trapped below the parent.
Reject: cancelled child work was part of the same exhausted fan-out chain and is not a separate takeover boundary with distinct anchors and consequence.
Reject: no completed child result is shown available to the parent and then ignored at a decision point.
Reject: the parent actively probed and wrote source while children ran; it did not simply wait through the deadline without inspection or progress.
Reject: there are no concurrently produced final-source files claiming overlapping behavior that required reconciliation.
Reject: no two live agents are shown editing the same final source file with an observed conflict.
Reject: no agent is shown replacing a non-entry source file produced or actively owned by another agent.
Reject: no build, copy, or edit replaced the required executable or entry point while another agent owned it.
Reject: no broad cleanup or promotion invalidated another agent’s final workspace outputs.
Reject: workflow children were instructed to use /tmp/work scratch directories, and no unstable final-workspace provenance problem is proven.
Reject: no generated temporary artifact from one concurrent actor is shown contaminating another actor’s reference environment or verification.
